title: 'Bed' language and bed icons are used for shops, warehouses and flats that have no beds
description: User-reported, and broader than LODGY-85 which fixes one screen. LODGY-79 let wardens keep shops, warehouses and flats, where the property itself is the rentable unit and its floor/room/bed rows exist only to keep the queries working. The UI still says 'bed' in places that now cover those properties, and draws a literal bed pictogram for them. CONFIRMED IN CODE. Home: the dashboard tile is R.string.dashboard_vacant_beds, 'Vacant beds' - the user asked for plain 'Vacant', which is both generic and shorter, and the count already spans every property since LODGY-81. The screen it opens is titled 'Vacant Beds' (vacant_view_title) and its rows read 'Room %1$s . Bed %2$s' (vacant_view_room_bed) with a '%2$d bed(s)' count per floor. Icons: StatusTokens maps both bed status and room fill onto StatusIcons.BedVacant / BedOccupied, which are drawn as a bed - so a shop tile in All rooms and a warehouse in the bed grid are labelled with a bed. Other strings in the same family: room_bed_summary, floor_bed_summary, bed_filter_vacant, bed_status_vacant. WHAT NOT TO DO: renaming everything to 'unit' would be worse. A hostel warden thinks in beds and that word is correct for them; the fix is generic wording where a figure spans both kinds, and property-appropriate wording where the screen knows which kind it is showing - the split BedGridScreen and AllRoomsScreen already make.
acceptanceCriteria: The Home tile reads 'Vacant' rather than 'Vacant beds', in both languages
A grid or tile for a shop, warehouse or flat does not show a bed icon
A screen that knows it is showing a single-unit property does not use the word bed anywhere on it
A hostel keeps bed wording and the bed icon, because that word is right for it
A figure that spans both kinds of property is worded so it is true of both
The vacant list reached from the Home tile is covered too, not just the tile
Correct in Hindi as well as English
No string is left saying 'bed' in a place a warehouse can appear

history.note: Filed from direct user feedback: 'the home screen shows vacant beds - change the label to Vacant to make it generic. Also in the grid - change the icons accordingly, and don't mention bed in non-bed cases.' Raised alongside LODGY-85, which covers the tenant onboarding picker; this one is the same vocabulary problem everywhere else.

Starting. Working from the split BedGridScreen and AllRoomsScreen already make - generic where a figure spans both kinds of property, property-appropriate where the screen knows which kind it is showing.

Built to the rule in the description - generic where a figure spans both kinds, property-appropriate where the screen knows which kind it is showing - rather than renaming everything to 'unit'. HOME: dashboard_vacant_beds is now 'Vacant' / 'खाली' (AC1). ICONS: two new StatusIcons, UnitVacant and UnitOccupied, drawn as a door rather than a bed. BedStatus.icon and RoomFill.icon became functions taking singleUnit, so a tile picks its own symbol: the Corner shop tile in All rooms and the shop's grid now carry a door, hostel rooms and beds still carry a bed (AC2, AC4). Added RoomFill.spaceIcon for the All-rooms summary row, which counts ROOMS across every property and so always uses the neutral door - deliberately not flipping with whatever the warden happens to own, since an icon that changes meaning based on portfolio composition is worse than one that is simply generic (AC5). WORDING: BedStatus.label now takes singleUnit too, which turned up a real gap - unit_status_vacant and unit_status_occupied ('Vacant' / 'Let') were DEFINED BUT NEVER USED, so a shop's tile and its action sheet were showing the bed wording 'VACANT' / 'OCCUPIED'. They are now used (AC3). FINDING THAT CHANGES AC6, please check this rather than take my word: there is no separate vacant list any more. The Home tile has routed to All rooms filtered to hasSpace since LODGY-72, and VACANT_VIEW_ROUTE - kept only so older notifications still land somewhere - renders AllRoomsScreen too. So all five vacant_view_* strings ('Vacant Beds', 'Room %1$s . Bed %2$s', '%2$d bed(s)' and two more) were dead resources. I deleted them rather than translating strings nothing renders; that is what covers AC6 and AC8. The user manual described that screen as though it still existed, and has been corrected. LEFT ALONE ON PURPOSE: room_bed_summary ('%1$d vacant / %2$d beds') and floor_bed_summary are on RoomListScreen and the floor cards, which a single-unit property can never reach - it goes straight to its own grid - so 'bed' is correct there and generic wording would be worse for the hostel warden who does see them (AC4). VERIFIED ON DEVICE: Home reads 'Vacant 46'. All rooms shows a door on Corner shop and beds on 501 and 101, with door icons in the 16 Empty / 1 Part full / 3 Full summary. The shop's grid reads 'This property / Let / ₹18000 per month' with no 'bed' anywhere, and its sheet 'Corner shop / Let / Occupied by Shop tenant'. Room 501 is unchanged: 'Bed A / OCCUPIED / ₹4000 per bed'. Hindi correct throughout - 'खाली', 'यह प्रॉपर्टी', 'किराये पर', '₹18000 / महीना' (AC7). TESTS: 3 new covering the per-property icon split and the neutral spanning icon, plus two existing assertions updated for the new signatures. Full suite 544 pass, 0 failures, coverage 95.93% line against the 0.93 gate. Not schema-affecting.
